definitions.explanation: A train powered by steam. This term is somewhat dated as steam trains are now rare in Japan.

examples.japanese: {汽車|きしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: I can hear the sound of the steam train.

examples.japanese: {汽車|きしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{煙|けむり}→煙：02705_kemuri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: I can see the smoke from the steam train.
Have you ever ridden a steam train?

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧{汽車|きしゃ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, everyone traveled by steam train.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時|とき}→時：02918_toki⟧、⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{汽車|きしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}った→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えている→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
examples.english: I remember riding the steam train with my grandfather when I was a child.

notes:
{汽車|きしゃ} refers specifically to steam-powered trains, which are now rare in modern Japan.

CONTRAST WITH OTHER TRAINS:
- {汽車|きしゃ}: steam train (steam-powered)
- {電車|でんしゃ}: electric train (most common today)
- {列車|れっしゃ}: train (general/formal term)
- {新幹線|しんかんせん}: bullet train

COMPOUNDS:
- {汽車|きしゃ}{賃|ちん}: train fare (dated)
- {蒸気|じょうき}{機関車|きかんしゃ}: steam locomotive (technical term)

REGIONAL NOTE:
In some rural areas, especially among older speakers, {汽車|きしゃ} may still be used colloquially to refer to any train, regardless of power source.

HOMOPHONE:
{記者|きしゃ} (journalist) has the same reading.
